title: EE-HPC a Framework for Energy Efficient HPC System Management
problem: Large-scale HPC data centers consume substantial energy with rising costs and environmental impact. Current systems lack targeted, job-specific hardware control to optimize energy usage based on application requirements.
motivation: Energy efficiency and carbon reduction are becoming critical operational and funding priorities for HPC data center providers.
method: EE-HPC monitors power use across hybrid HPC clusters (systems with mixed processor types) using tools called ClusterCockpit and LIKWID. The framework detects when a program switches between different computational phases and automatically adjusts hardware power settings in response. This dynamic tuning applies to MPI (code distributed across multiple computers) and OpenMP (code running in parallel on one computer) regions. Testing involved molecular dynamics and earth system modeling simulations.
key_novelty: The framework automatically adjusts hardware power settings based on each program's computational phase, instead of using the same settings for all work.
contributions: Energy-aware software components for real-time power monitoring and energy consumption reduction
Scalable monitoring and energy control framework for hybrid HPC cluster management
Instrumentation library for fine-grained phase detection and dynamic tuning of parallel regions
Evaluation on diverse HPC applications demonstrating framework effectiveness
limitations: The abstract does not discuss limitations or constraints of the framework.
primary_theme: energy-efficient HPC cluster management through targeted job optimization
